records.title: Escitalopram
records.summary: Once-daily SSRI for depression or anxiety that persists on a long mission.

data.spaceflight_note: NASA lists adverse behavioral conditions and psychiatric disorders as a risk for long-duration exploration missions; escitalopram is a once-daily SSRI for depression and generalized anxiety, a second option if sertraline is not tolerated.
data.cautions: Takes several weeks to work fully. Watch for suicidal thoughts early on, low sodium, bleeding risk with NSAIDs or aspirin, and serotonin syndrome with tramadol, sumatriptan or other serotonergic drugs. Do not stop suddenly.
data.dosing: See the dose reference (label-sourced) in the Pharmacy tab.

records.title: Buspirone
records.summary: Non-sedating, non-habit-forming treatment for ongoing anxiety.

data.spaceflight_note: Treats ongoing anxiety without the sedation, dependence or performance impairment of benzodiazepines, so a crewmember can keep working, including on safety-critical tasks.
data.cautions: Takes several weeks to reach a working dose; not for acute panic. Dizziness, nausea, headache. Do not combine with MAOIs; grapefruit and some antifungals or antibiotics raise levels.
data.dosing: See the dose reference (label-sourced) in the Pharmacy tab.

records.title: Propranolol
records.summary: Beta blocker for situational anxiety symptoms, fast heart rhythms and migraine prevention.
tags: Fast heart rate in atrial fibrillation

uses: Fast heart rate in atrial fibrillation
data.spaceflight_note: Blunts the adrenaline-driven racing heart and tremor of situational anxiety before high-stakes events without sedation; also covers atrial fibrillation rate control and migraine prevention. Beta blockade can worsen the orthostatic intolerance seen after landing or a gravity transition.
data.cautions: Do not use with asthma, slow heart rate, heart block or shock. Can hide low blood sugar warning signs and blunt the response to epinephrine. Do not stop suddenly after regular use. Situational anxiety is an off-label use in the U.S.
data.dosing: See the dose reference (label-sourced) in the Pharmacy tab.

records.title: Mirtazapine
records.summary: Sedating bedtime antidepressant that also helps sleep and appetite.
tags: Depression with poor sleep or appetite

uses: Depression with poor sleep or appetite
data.spaceflight_note: Taken at bedtime, it helps depression together with poor sleep and poor appetite, both common problems on long missions; the dissolving tablet needs no water.
data.cautions: Strong drowsiness, weight gain, raised cholesterol. Rarely a very low white cell count: report fever or sore throat. Serotonin syndrome risk with other serotonergic drugs. Do not stop suddenly.
data.dosing: See the dose reference (label-sourced) in the Pharmacy tab.

records.title: Olanzapine
records.summary: Antipsychotic for acute severe agitation or psychosis, by injection or dissolving tablet.

data.spaceflight_note: Behavioral emergency backup to haloperidol: a confined crew cannot isolate or evacuate an agitated member, the IM form works when the person cannot cooperate, and the dissolving tablet needs no water.
data.cautions: Low blood pressure on standing, slow heart rate, heavy sedation. Do not combine IM olanzapine with injected benzodiazepines (lorazepam, midazolam, diazepam). Raises blood sugar and weight with longer use.
data.dosing: See the dose reference (label-sourced) in the Pharmacy tab.

records.title: Diltiazem
records.summary: IV calcium channel blocker for fast control of a rapid irregular heartbeat.

data.spaceflight_note: Atrial fibrillation has been documented in astronauts; IV diltiazem gives fast heart-rate control, complementing adenosine (to convert SVT) and amiodarone already in the kit.
data.cautions: Medical officer only, with ECG and blood pressure monitoring. Causes low blood pressure and slow heart rate. Not for heart block, sick sinus, WPW with atrial fibrillation or wide-QRS tachycardia. Do not give within a few hours of an IV beta blocker.
data.dosing: See the dose reference (label-sourced) in the Pharmacy tab.

records.title: Labetalol
records.summary: IV alpha and beta blocker for dangerously high blood pressure.

data.spaceflight_note: Controlled stepwise IV lowering of dangerously high blood pressure, for example with a head injury or bleeding, where nitroglycerin alone is not enough.
data.cautions: Keep the patient lying down during and for up to 3 hours after IV doses; blood pressure falls a lot on standing or on return to gravity. Not for asthma, heart failure, heart block or slow heart rate.
data.dosing: See the dose reference (label-sourced) in the Pharmacy tab.

records.title: Amoxicillin
records.summary: First-choice narrow-spectrum antibiotic for dental, ear, sinus and chest infections.

data.spaceflight_note: WHO Model List of Essential Medicines Access-group antibiotic and first choice for many common infections including dental ones; narrower than amoxicillin-clavulanate, which spares the crew microbiome and limits resistance in a closed habitat.
data.cautions: Do not use with penicillin allergy. Rash, diarrhea; watch for C. difficile diarrhea. Lower dose in severe kidney disease.
data.dosing: See the dose reference (label-sourced) in the Pharmacy tab.

records.title: Fosfomycin
records.summary: Single-dose antibiotic for a simple bladder infection.

data.form: Granules for oral solution (3 g sachet)
data.spaceflight_note: Urinary tract infections occur in spaceflight (fluid shifts, urinary retention, catheter use); one sachet treats cystitis when nitrofurantoin is unsuitable, and a single dose keeps stock small.
data.cautions: Not for kidney infection (fever, flank pain). Diarrhea, nausea, headache. One dose only; do not repeat without medical advice. Must be dissolved in cold water first.
data.dosing: See the dose reference (label-sourced) in the Pharmacy tab.

records.title: Ertapenem
records.summary: Once-daily broad-spectrum injectable antibiotic for serious abdominal and skin infections.
tags: Complicated abdominal infection (e.g. appendicitis without surgery)

uses: Complicated abdominal infection (e.g. appendicitis without surgery)
data.spaceflight_note: Once-daily IV or IM broad-spectrum cover; ertapenem was the antibiotic used in the APPAC trial of antibiotics-first treatment of uncomplicated appendicitis, relevant where surgery is impossible.
data.cautions: Medical officer only. Not with serious beta-lactam allergy. Can cause seizures and lowers valproate levels. C. difficile diarrhea. Lower dose in severe kidney disease.
data.dosing: See the dose reference (label-sourced) in the Pharmacy tab.

records.title: Methylprednisolone (IV/IM)
records.summary: Injectable steroid for severe allergic reactions and severe asthma after first-line treatment.
tags: Severe allergic reaction or anaphylaxis (adjunct after epinephrine)

data.form: Injection (powder for IV or IM use)
uses: Severe allergic reaction or anaphylaxis (adjunct after epinephrine)
data.spaceflight_note: Injectable steroid for when swallowing or gut absorption is unreliable; used after epinephrine in anaphylaxis and severe asthma, and works IM if no IV line is available.
data.cautions: Never a substitute for epinephrine. Raises blood sugar; mood and sleep changes. Rapid large IV doses can cause heart rhythm problems.
data.dosing: See the dose reference (label-sourced) in the Pharmacy tab.

records.title: Ketorolac eye drops
records.summary: NSAID eye drops for itchy allergic eyes and eye inflammation.

data.spaceflight_note: Floating dust and debris in the cabin make eye irritation a frequent spaceflight complaint; a non-steroid drop eases itch and inflammation without the infection risk of steroid drops.
data.cautions: Stinging on instillation. Do not use while wearing contact lenses. Long use can slow corneal healing. Wait 5 minutes between different eye drops.
data.dosing: See the dose reference (label-sourced) in the Pharmacy tab.

records.title: Triamcinolone cream
records.summary: Medium-strength steroid cream for rashes that hydrocortisone does not control.

data.spaceflight_note: Skin rashes and hypersensitivity reactions are among the most common complaints on long-duration ISS missions; this medium-strength steroid treats rashes that hydrocortisone 1% cannot control.
data.cautions: Thin film only. Avoid face, groin, armpits and broken or infected skin. Skin thinning with long use. Not for fungal infections.
data.dosing: See the dose reference (label-sourced) in the Pharmacy tab.

records.title: Potassium iodide
records.summary: Thyroid blocker taken only after a release of radioactive iodine.
tags: Thyroid protection after release of radioactive iodine

uses: Thyroid protection after release of radioactive iodine
data.spaceflight_note: Protects the thyroid only from radioactive iodine, for example after a fission surface-power or nuclear-propulsion accident. It gives no protection from solar particle events or galactic cosmic rays.
data.cautions: Take only when directed, at most one dose in 24 hours. Do not take with iodine allergy, dermatitis herpetiformis, hypocomplementemic vasculitis, or nodular thyroid disease with heart disease. Protects no other organ.
data.dosing: See the dose reference (label-sourced) in the Pharmacy tab.

records.title: Filgrastim
records.summary: Bone marrow growth factor after a dangerous radiation dose.

data.spaceflight_note: FDA-approved to increase survival after myelosuppressive radiation doses (above 2 Gy). Justified only as a contingency for an extreme solar particle event during EVA or outside the storm shelter; it needs refrigeration and has a limited shelf life.
data.cautions: Medical officer only. Bone pain. Rarely spleen rupture (left upper belly or shoulder pain), lung injury, allergic reaction. Needs blood counts to guide use.
data.dosing: See the dose reference (label-sourced) in the Pharmacy tab.

records.title: Bethanechol
records.summary: Helps the bladder empty when urine retention is not caused by a blockage.

data.spaceflight_note: Urinary retention is common early in spaceflight (altered bladder sensation, anticholinergic motion-sickness drugs); bethanechol can help the bladder empty and reduce catheter use. Complements tamsulosin.
data.cautions: Never use if a blockage is possible. Not for asthma, slow heart rate, low blood pressure, peptic ulcer, coronary disease, overactive thyroid or epilepsy. Take on an empty stomach. Atropine reverses it.
data.dosing: See the dose reference (label-sourced) in the Pharmacy tab.

records.title: Sodium fluoride 1.1% toothpaste
records.summary: High-fluoride prescription toothpaste to prevent tooth decay when no dentist is available.

data.spaceflight_note: No dentist for months: high-fluoride toothpaste lowers decay risk from frequent snacking, limited fresh food and dry mouth caused by antihistamines or scopolamine, reducing the chance of a dental emergency.
data.cautions: Spit out after brushing; do not swallow. Use in place of regular toothpaste. Not for children under 6.
data.dosing: See the dose reference (label-sourced) in the Pharmacy tab.

records.title: Sumatriptan
records.summary: Tablet that stops a migraine attack.

data.spaceflight_note: Headache is one of the most common spaceflight complaints, partly linked to cabin CO2; sumatriptan treats true migraine attacks that acetaminophen or NSAIDs do not stop.
data.cautions: Not with heart disease, uncontrolled high blood pressure, stroke or TIA history. Chest or throat tightness. Serotonin syndrome risk with SSRIs. Do not use headache medicines more than 10 days a month.
data.dosing: See the dose reference (label-sourced) in the Pharmacy tab.

records.title: Acetazolamide
records.summary: Lowers eye pressure in acute glaucoma and prevents altitude illness.

data.spaceflight_note: Lowers eye pressure in an angle-closure glaucoma emergency when no eye surgeon is available, and prevents altitude illness in reduced-pressure habitat atmospheres. Not approved for spaceflight-associated neuro-ocular syndrome (SANS).
data.cautions: Sulfa-type allergy cross-reaction. Tingling, frequent urination, low potassium and acid buildup. Not for low sodium or potassium, marked kidney or liver disease, or cirrhosis.
data.dosing: See the dose reference (label-sourced) in the Pharmacy tab.

records.title: Vancomycin (oral)
records.summary: Gut-only antibiotic capsule for C. difficile diarrhea.
tags: Glycopeptide antibiotic (oral, stays in the gut)

data.drug_class: Glycopeptide antibiotic (oral, stays in the gut)
data.spaceflight_note: Antibiotic courses in a closed habitat raise the risk of C. difficile colitis, whose spores spread on shared surfaces; oral vancomycin stays in the gut and treats it.
data.cautions: Oral capsules do not treat infections outside the gut. Nausea, belly pain. Strict hand washing; alcohol gel does not kill C. difficile spores.
data.dosing: See the dose reference (label-sourced) in the Pharmacy tab.
